sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:31

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:31:1
items.html: In this sight there is direct light and reflected light: For the expansion of the upper light to the Partzuf is called sight. And that part of the light which is received in the Partzuf is called direct light, that is, down to the vessel of Malchut. And that part of the light which is not received in the Partzuf, because of the screen that returns it backwards — that is, the part that was fit to clothe in Malchut — is called reflected light. And this is what he says: in this sight there is direct light and reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:31:2
items.html: And in the looking of this sight, in the aspect of direct light, in the light of Nefesh: Meaning in Malchut, which is called Nefesh. And the light of Nefesh is the reflected light that she raises upward from herself and that clothes the upper light, in the aspect of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head]. And this is what he says: there was sufficient capacity to make the vessels of the GAR [first three]. That is, the vessels of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, which are from below upward, which are regarded as the roots of the vessels, as is known.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:31:3
items.html: The seven lower vessels were not completed, etc., until the vessel of the tenth Malchut. Which is called Malchut of Malchut, or Nefesh of Nefesh. For the above Malchut of the Rosh, which is called Nefesh, or “Et,” expanded of herself into ten Sefirot from her and within her, down to her own Malchut, that is, Malchut of Malchut. And these ten Sefirot are called Guf [body], or the seven lower Sefirot. And in AK they are called Akudim, which expand from the Peh [mouth] of AK down to his Tabur. For the Malchut of the Rosh is called Peh, and Malchut of Malchut is called Tabur.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:31:4
items.html: The light of the sight of the eye, and the light of Nefesh that came out of the Peh. Meaning the direct light and the reflected light, for the light of sight is direct light, and the light of Nefesh is the reflected light that rises from Malchut, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:31:5
items.html:
And both of them returned to depart upward, from below upward, etc., the seven lower vessels were made in the secret of the reflected light. And this is through the refinement of the screen, as was written at length above in Part 4. For when the screen refines from phase four to phase three, the coupling on phase four ceases, and the reflected light, together with the direct light of the level of Keter within it, depart and rise upward, and the coupling is made on phase three, which is the aspect of ZA of direct light, whose reflected light connects and clothes only the level of Hochma. And the light of Hochma comes into the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina into the vessel of Hochma, and the light of ZA into the vessel of Bina, and the light of Malchut into the vessel of ZA, and the vessel of Malchut remains without light. And then the vessel of Malchut darkens and thickens and becomes a vessel, as above in the words of the ARI, item 27, study it there well. And likewise afterwards, when the screen refines from phase three to phase two, which is Bina of direct light, and the reflected light and the direct light of the level of Hochma depart, and the level of Bina is drawn — for then the light of Bina clothes in the vessel of Keter, and the light of ZA in the vessel of Hochma, and the light of Malchut in the vessel of Bina, and the vessel of ZA, too, remains without light — then the vessel of ZA darkens and thickens, and thereby becomes a vessel, as above in the words of the ARI. And when it refines from phase two to phase one, which is Hochma of direct light, and the level of Bina departs and the level of ZA is drawn, and the light of ZA comes into the vessel of Keter, and the vessel of Bina, too, remains without light — then the vessel of Bina, too, darkens and thickens. And so forth in this manner. Thus the vessels of the Guf are made only through the departure of the direct light and the reflected light upward, for then they darken and thicken and become vessels.
However, only the two vessels of ZA and of Malchut were entirely completed by this departure, both their inner half, for the inner light, and their outer half, for the surrounding light. (As above, page 311, in the Inner Light, the passage beginning “that it grow distant,” study it there well.) But the three vessels — Keter, Hochma, Bina — were not yet completed here by this departure, since they still lack the outer halves of the walls of the vessels, for they had no ascents at all for the attainment of vessels and surrounding lights, as above. Therefore they were completed only afterwards, in the second expansion, as is written before us.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:31:6
items.html: But the first three vessels were made by direct light from above downward, through the look of the direct light of the Eynaim [eyes] in the light of Nefesh. That is, the vessels of the GAR, which are of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, were made through the expansion of the direct light from above downward to a coupling by striking in Malchut, where Malchut raised reflected light from below upward and clothed the direct light of the Eynaim, as the ARI wrote at length at the beginning of Part 3, study it there.
